Definition: apparently a primary word; a "mother" (literally or figuratively, immediate or remote):--mother.
BiblicalUsage: Mary the mother of Jesus stands at the cross, Mary and the brethren wait outside while Jesus teaches, the church prays with Mary the mother of Jesus after the ascension, and Paul says the Jerusalem above is the mother of us all. The word stretches from one woman to the whole people of God.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe motherhood in Scripture is bigger than biology: Mary bore the Lord, the church bears His children, and the Jerusalem above mothers us all until we come home. That is why motherhood is holy ground in Scripture, not just biology.
